title: Viscoelastic Characterization of Soft Tissue-Mimicking Gelatin Phantoms using Indentation and Magnetic Resonance Elastography
protocol: Weigh gelatin, glycerol, and water according to Table 1.
Mix the gelatin powder with water to obtain the gelatin solution.
Heat the gelatin solution to 60 °C in a water bath.
Add glycerol to the heated gelatin solution while maintaining the temperature at 60 °C.
Stir the solution and heat it again to 60 °C.
Pour the mixed solution into a container for MRE and indentation tests.
Cool the solution to room temperature until solidified.
Place the vibration plate on top of the gelatin phantom.
Ensure firm contact between the phantom and the vibration plate.
Place the gelatin phantom into the head coil.
Put sponges and sandbags around the phantom to ensure it is firmly placed.
Mount an electromagnetic actuator on the head coil.
Connect the transmission bar to the vibration plate.
Connect the power lines of the actuator with the amplifier.
Connect the control lines with the controller.
Set the waveform to sinusoidal in the function generator.
Set the vibration frequency to 40 Hz or 50 Hz.
Set the amplitude to 1.5 Vpp in the function generator.
Adjust the power amplifier amplification ratio to 40%.
Connect the trigger line to the external trigger port of the MRI machine.
Set the MRE scanning frequency the same as that from the function generator.
Use a 2D gradient-echo (GRE) based MRE sequence for imaging.
Set the GRE-MRE imaging parameters: Flip-angle = 30°; TR/TE = 50/31 ms.
Set the field-of-view to 300 mm, slice thickness to 5 mm, and voxel size to 2.34 x 2.34 mm².
Measure phase images at four temporal points in one sinusoidal cycle.
Apply both positive and negative motion encoding gradients at each time point.
Remove background phase by subtracting the positive and negative encoded phase images.
Unwrap the phase with a reliability sorting-based algorithm.
Apply fast Fourier Transform to the unwrapped phase images to extract the principal component of motion.
Filter the phase image with a digital bandpass filter set at [0.04 0.08].
Estimate the shear modulus using a 2D direct inversion algorithm with a fitting window size of 11 x 11 to obtain storage modulus G' and loss modulus G''.
Trim the gelatin phantom into a cylindrical or cuboid sample using a circular punch or surgical blade.
Ensure the sample thickness is between 3 and 10 mm, and that the diameter of the cylindrical sample or long side of the cuboid is larger than 4 mm.
Smooth the surface of the sample with a sharp blade before indentation testing.
Turn on the power of the indentation tester.
Initiate the calibration process by clicking on the Back off button in the GUI.
Read the value from the laser sensor and enter it into the BaseLine box.
Place a glass slide on the baffle plate.
Record the value shown by the laser sensor.
Put the sample on the glass slide.
Place the glass slide with the sample on the baffle plate.
Read the value from the laser sensor and type this value in the Sample+Slide box.
Take the difference between the two values obtained to calculate the sample thickness at the region of interest (ROI).
Carefully place the sample along with the underlying glass slide right below the indenter.
Click on the Contact button to initiate automatic contact between the indenter and the sample surface.
If the automatic contact is not satisfactory, adjust the indenter position by typing a value in the range of 0.05-0.1 mm in the Offset box.
Repeat steps from placing the glass slide on the baffle plate up to initiating automatic contact.
Based on the measured sample thickness (step 3.2.3), estimate the indentation displacement by multiplying the thickness with the indented testing strain (≤8%).
Type the displacement values in the Displacement (mm) box.
Set the relaxation time to 180 s in the Dwell Time box.
Click on the Indentation button.
Export the indentation data to a spreadsheet.
